newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan overnight rate hits 0.51%, highest since Oct.
newsitem.headline: Japan overnight rate hits 0.51%, highest since Oct.

text.p: The weighted average of Japan"s key interbank overnight call rate rose to 0.51 percent on Wednesday, its highest level since October 1, 1996, money traders said.
A lack of issues of long-term certificates of deposit (CDs) recently has been putting upward pressure on the benchmark rate in the short-end of the market, traders said.
The rate was mainly traded at 0.51 percent on Wednesday, although a few banks raised funds at 0.52. Tuesday"s weighted average was 0.50 percent.

This suggested the spread of fund-raising costs among Japanese banks was widening. But whether the key overnight rate"s weighted average would stay above 0.50 in the future was not known, traders said.
"I was wondering why they (some banks) were in such a hurry, because the Bank of Japan"s operation remained neutral today," said a city bank dealer.

Some banks, including major city banks, which were short of funds on Wednesday hurried to raise overnight money at 0.51 percent early in the morning, and this became a trend, a trust bank dealer said.
